paragraphs.text: Yi Ji (一级) is the [first grade](yi-ji:definition) of Anhua's numbered raw leaf. Leaf there is sorted by how tender it was when picked, and this is the most tender of the numbered lots; each higher number means older, coarser leaf. A grade describes the leaf that went in, [not how the tea was made](yi-ji:grade-and-quality) or which garden it came from.

[Anhua](anhua:where-it-is) is a mountain county on the Zi river in north-central Hunan, at the northern foot of the Xuefeng mountains, and is widely named as the main home of [Anhua dark tea](anhua-dark:definition) and of [dark tea](dark:definition) in China. In dark tea, the leaf keeps changing in warmth and moisture after it is made. Here the same [warm, wet air](anhua:why-people-value-it) that grows the leaf is the air it is piled and aged in, which is why the trade ties the finished tea to the place as well as to the method.
This leaf is from 2015 and is now eleven years old. Anhua tea is [kept for years](anhua-dark:ageing) and is said to improve as it ages, though no agreed number of years marks it as aged.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: A redder liquor, a sweeter, mellower cup, and sometimes a medicinal or herbal note.
